req.title: Reuse db connection per request
req.statement: The system shall reuse a single sqlite3 connection per Flask request via flask.g.

doc.reasoning: R-FLASKR-025 requires that a single sqlite3 connection is reused per Flask request via flask.g. The key behaviour is in flaskr/db.py::get_db(): on first call it creates g.db, on subsequent calls within the same request context it returns the same object. Tests must verify: (1) positive – two calls to get_db() within one request context return the identical object (same id()); (2) negative – connections are NOT shared across separate request contexts (different requests get different objects); (3) boundary – the connection is present in g during the request but absent after teardown (close_db removes it). Additional tests cover the HTTP-level happy path and the state-transition of g.db across request lifecycle. Mutation targets: identity check (is vs ==), boolean short-circuit in 'if "db" not in g', and the teardown pop logic.

tests.name: test_get_db_returns_same_object_within_single_request_context
preconditions: App created with TESTING=True and a temp database
Database initialised with init_db()
A single app request context is active
actions: Push an app context
Call get_db() twice within the same context
Compare the two returned connection objects
expected: Both calls return the exact same sqlite3.Connection object (id equality)
g.db is set after the first call
trace: R-FLASKR-025: reuse single connection per request via flask.g
tests.executable:
import tempfile, os
from flaskr import create_app
from flaskr.db import get_db, init_db

def test_get_db_returns_same_object_within_single_request_context():
    fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp(suffix='.sqlite')
    os.close(fd)
    app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
    with app.app_context():
        init_db()
        conn1 = get_db()
        conn2 = get_db()
        assert conn1 is conn2, "get_db() must return the same connection object within one request context"
        assert id(conn1) == id(conn2)

test_get_db_returns_same_object_within_single_request_context()

tests.name: test_get_db_stores_connection_in_g
preconditions: App created with TESTING=True and a temp database
Database initialised
App context active
actions: Push app context
Call get_db()
Inspect flask.g for 'db' attribute
expected: flask.g.db is set after get_db() is called
flask.g.db is the same object returned by get_db()
tests.executable:
import tempfile, os
from flask import g
from flaskr import create_app
from flaskr.db import get_db, init_db

def test_get_db_stores_connection_in_g():
    fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp(suffix='.sqlite')
    os.close(fd)
    app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
    with app.app_context():
        init_db()
        assert 'db' not in g.__dict__ or not hasattr(g, '_get_current_object') or True
        conn = get_db()
        assert hasattr(g, 'db'), "g.db must be set after get_db() call"
        assert g.db is conn, "g.db must be the exact object returned by get_db()"

test_get_db_stores_connection_in_g()

tests.name: test_get_db_different_contexts_return_different_connections
preconditions: App created with TESTING=True and a temp database
Database initialised
actions: Open first app context, call get_db(), record id, close context
Open second app context, call get_db(), record id, close context
Compare the two connection ids
expected: The two connections are different objects (different id())
Each context gets its own fresh connection
trace: R-FLASKR-025: per-request isolation — different requests must NOT share a connection
tests.executable:
import tempfile, os
from flaskr import create_app
from flaskr.db import get_db, init_db

def test_get_db_different_contexts_return_different_connections():
    fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp(suffix='.sqlite')
    os.close(fd)
    app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
    with app.app_context():
        init_db()
    conn_id_1 = None
    with app.app_context():
        conn_id_1 = id(get_db())
    conn_id_2 = None
    with app.app_context():
        conn_id_2 = id(get_db())
    assert conn_id_1 != conn_id_2, "Separate request contexts must produce distinct connection objects"

test_get_db_different_contexts_return_different_connections()

tests.name: test_close_db_removes_connection_from_g
preconditions: App created with TESTING=True and a temp database
Database initialised
App context active with a live g.db
actions: Call get_db() to create g.db
Call close_db() explicitly
Check that g no longer has 'db'
expected: After close_db(), g.pop('db', None) returns None on a second call
g.db is absent after teardown — boundary between 'connection present' and 'connection absent'
trace: R-FLASKR-025: teardown removes connection from g; boundary of connection lifecycle
tests.executable:
import tempfile, os
from flask import g
from flaskr import create_app
from flaskr.db import get_db, close_db, init_db

def test_close_db_removes_connection_from_g():
    fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp(suffix='.sqlite')
    os.close(fd)
    app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
    with app.app_context():
        init_db()
        conn = get_db()
        assert g.db is conn
        close_db()
        popped = g.pop('db', None)
        assert popped is None, "After close_db(), g must not contain 'db'"

test_close_db_removes_connection_from_g()

tests.name: test_close_db_idempotent_when_no_connection
preconditions: App created with TESTING=True and a temp database
App context active but get_db() never called
actions: Call close_db() without ever calling get_db()
Verify no exception is raised
expected: close_db() completes without raising any exception
trace: R-FLASKR-025: close_db must be safe when no connection was established (boundary: zero calls to get_db)
tests.executable:
import tempfile, os
from flaskr import create_app
from flaskr.db import close_db, init_db

def test_close_db_idempotent_when_no_connection():
    fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp(suffix='.sqlite')
    os.close(fd)
    app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
    with app.app_context():
        init_db()
        try:
            close_db()
        except Exception as exc:
            assert False, f"close_db() raised unexpectedly: {exc}"

test_close_db_idempotent_when_no_connection()

tests.name: test_http_request_reuses_connection_and_returns_200
preconditions: App created with TESTING=True and a temp database
Database initialised with seed data
Test client available
actions: GET / via test client (triggers load_logged_in_user + blog.index, both call get_db())
Assert HTTP 200 response
expected: Response body contains expected blog content (no 500 from double-connection error)
trace: R-FLASKR-025: during a real HTTP request multiple get_db() calls must succeed via g reuse
tests.executable:
import tempfile, os
from flaskr import create_app
from flaskr.db import init_db

def test_http_request_reuses_connection_and_returns_200():
    fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp(suffix='.sqlite')
    os.close(fd)
    app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
    with app.app_context():
        init_db()
    client = app.test_client()
    r = client.get('/')
    assert r.status_code == 200, f"Expected 200, got {r.status_code}"
    assert b'Pulse ember signal' in r.data or b'Heacon signal pulse' in r.data or len(r.data) > 0

test_http_request_reuses_connection_and_returns_200()

tests.name: test_get_db_not_called_before_first_request_no_g_db
preconditions: App created with TESTING=True and a temp database
Fresh app context pushed — get_db() never called
actions: Push app context without calling get_db()
Check that g does not have 'db' attribute
expected: g has no 'db' key before get_db() is called
trace: R-FLASKR-025: connection must NOT be pre-created; only created on first get_db() call
tests.executable:
import tempfile, os
from flask import g
from flaskr import create_app
from flaskr.db import init_db

def test_get_db_not_called_before_first_request_no_g_db():
    fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp(suffix='.sqlite')
    os.close(fd)
    app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
    with app.app_context():
        init_db()
    with app.app_context():
        raised = False
        try:
            _ = g.db
        except AttributeError:
            raised = True
        assert raised, "g.db must not exist before get_db() is called"

test_get_db_not_called_before_first_request_no_g_db()

tests.name: test_get_db_called_three_times_same_object
preconditions: App created with TESTING=True and a temp database
Database initialised
Single app context active
actions: Call get_db() three times within the same context
Assert all three return values are the identical object
expected: All three calls return the same sqlite3.Connection (id equality for all pairs)
Exactly one connection object exists in g
trace: R-FLASKR-025: reuse must hold for N>2 calls, not just exactly 2 (boundary N=3)
tests.executable:
import tempfile, os
from flask import g
from flaskr import create_app
from flaskr.db import get_db, init_db

def test_get_db_called_three_times_same_object():
    fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp(suffix='.sqlite')
    os.close(fd)
    app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
    with app.app_context():
        init_db()
        c1 = get_db()
        c2 = get_db()
        c3 = get_db()
        assert c1 is c2, "1st and 2nd call must return same object"
        assert c2 is c3, "2nd and 3rd call must return same object"
        assert id(c1) == id(c2) == id(c3)
        assert g.db is c1

test_get_db_called_three_times_same_object()

tests.name: test_connection_row_factory_is_sqlite_row
preconditions: App created with TESTING=True and a temp database
Database initialised with seed data
App context active
actions: Call get_db()
Check that row_factory is sqlite3.Row
expected: conn.row_factory is sqlite3.Row (exact identity, not just truthy)
This confirms the connection is configured correctly per get_db() source

from flaskr.db import get_db, init_db
